questions.question: How should you do a driver-side parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Back past the parking space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the parking space without passing it first.
Back into the parking space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on your left. Then back into it. Bring the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: What can drivers do during the basic control skills test?

options.text: Cannot stop and exit to check the vehicle's position.
Should avoid exiting to check the vehicle's position.
Can exit the vehicle only if it is in reverse.
Can exit the vehicle if it is in neutral and the parking brake is set.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can exit the vehicle if it is in neutral and the parking brake is set.
questions.explanation: Place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake before exiting. You may check the vehicle's position no more than twice. For straight line backing, you may check only once.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a curve on the skills test?

options.text: Leave your lane if needed to complete the curve.
Slow down after entering the curve.
Don't look for other vehicles while turning.
Slow down before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before you enter the curve. Do not brake or shift once you are in the curve. Keep your vehicle in its lane. Check for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: What should a driver see in properly adjusted outside convex mirrors on a bus?

options.text: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
The front of the bus.
The rear door of the bus.
The top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors should show at least one traffic lane on each side of the bus, the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

questions.question: How many seconds before a bus stop should you turn on warning lights?

options.text: One to two seconds
Two to four seconds
Five to ten seconds
45 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Five to ten seconds
questions.explanation: Turn on alternating amber warning lights at least 200 feet before the stop. This gives about five to ten seconds of warning.

questions.question: What should you do during the on-road driving test?

options.text: Create your own route to show your driving skills.
Follow the examiner's directions.
Bring a passenger with you.
Drive in an unsafe way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the examiner's directions.
questions.explanation: Listen to and follow the examiner's directions. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: What can you be asked to do during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.
Drive in a figure eight.
Alley dock.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alley dock.
questions.explanation: Test maneuvers include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Which situation causes the most student deaths per year?

options.text: Students getting on or off a school bus
Accidents caused by drunk drivers
Accidents caused by negligence
Accidents caused by ignoring traffic signals or signs

questions.correctAnswerText: Students getting on or off a school bus
questions.explanation: More students die while loading or unloading school buses than while riding as passengers.

questions.question: For exercises other than straight line backing, how many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position?

options.text: One time.
Two times.
Three times.
Four times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two times.
questions.explanation: You can exit to check your vehicle's position during any exercise. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you may look only once. For all other exercises, you may look up to two times.

questions.question: What should a driver do if a student is missing after exiting the bus?

options.text: Secure the bus and look for the student.
Assume the student safely exited the bus.
Walk to the back of the bus to check if the student got back on.
Ask another student if they've seen the missing student.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the bus and look for the student.
questions.explanation: If you cannot find a student after they exit, secure the bus immediately. Check around and underneath the bus for the missing student.

questions.question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:

options.text: Be swept clean.
Contain rags.
Not be used for cargo.
Be free of cracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be free of cracks.
questions.explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer, check the front area for damage. Look for cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: A pull-up always counts against the applicant.
A pull-up should be completed at least once.
Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
Excessive pull-ups are acceptable in the opinions of some test administrators.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
questions.explanation: A pull-up happens when you stop and pull forward to get a better position. Stopping without moving forward is not a pull-up. Too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, a driver should make sure all nearby traffic has stopped before:

options.text: Opening the door and signaling for students to approach the bus.
Turning on the alternating red lights.
Pulling over to the side of the road.
Braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the door and signaling for students to approach the bus.
questions.explanation: When stopping to pick up students, wait until all nearby traffic has stopped. Then open the door and signal the students to come to the bus.

questions.question: When checking the springs during a vehicle inspection, do all of the following, except:

options.text: Look for missing leaf springs.
Look for broken coil springs.
Make sure torsion springs are not damaged.
Glue cracked leaf springs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glue cracked leaf springs.
questions.explanation: Check springs for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs. Look for broken or bent coil springs. Make sure torsion bars and torque arms are not damaged and are mounted securely. Do not glue cracked springs.

questions.question: Your vehicle's final position should be:

options.text: Exactly where the examiner has instructed it to be.
Within five feet of the final position described by the examiner.
Wherever you can safely park.
Within two feet of the final position described by the examiner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exactly where the examiner has instructed it to be.
questions.explanation: Park your vehicle exactly where the examiner tells you to park. Not following instructions exactly can result in failing the basic control skills test.

questions.question: Which of the following is not acceptable emergency equipment?

options.text: Three red reflective triangles
Six fuses
Three liquid burning flares
Four yellow squares

questions.correctAnswerText: Four yellow squares
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes spare fuses, either three red reflective triangles, six fuses, or three liquid burning flares, and a fully charged fire extinguisher. Yellow squares are not acceptable emergency equipment.

questions.question: When you are approaching a bus stop, the students on your bus should:

options.text: Remain seated.
Stand up and collect their belongings.
Walk to the front of the bus and prepare to exit.
Ask the driver questions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remain seated.
questions.explanation: Students must stay seated while the bus is moving. It is not safe for students to walk around the bus.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be required to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Walk around the vehicle.
Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.
Crawl under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crawl under the vehicle.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, walk around the vehicle and point to or touch each item. Explain what you are checking and why. You do not need to crawl under the vehicle or under the hood.

questions.question: A blind spot extends at least ____ behind a school bus.

options.text: 10 feet
50 feet
100 feet
1,000 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 feet
questions.explanation: School buses have blind spots next to the side mirrors and directly behind the rear bumper. The rear blind spot typically extends 50 to 150 feet behind the bus, but can sometimes reach 400 feet depending on the bus length.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, be sure that:

options.text: The emergency exits are difficult to open.
The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
The emergency exits squeak.
The emergency exits are not accessible from inside the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
questions.explanation: Make sure all emergency exit warning devices work. All emergency exits should open smoothly, be in good condition, and close securely from inside the bus.
